subject: Human Evolution
title: Farming's Trade-Off
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Farming's Trade-Off.

hook.text: The shift to farming 10,000 years ago is called a revolution. But early farmers were shorter and sicker.

buildup.text: Grain monocultures provided calories but lacked the nutrient variety of a foraging diet.

discovery.text: Skeletons from early farming sites show more cavities, anemia, and stunted growth than hunter-gatherers.

twist.text: Farming won not because it was healthier, but because it fed more mouths per acre—quantity over quality.

climax.text: More people survived, but individual health declined. Agriculture was a demographic win and a nutritional loss.

quiz.question: How did early farming affect individual health?
options: Nutrition declined but more people could be fed
